examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
A bridge increases component count when removed. An articulation vertex can increase it when removed with incident edges. A tree is connected and acyclic, with V−1 edges; an edge count alone does not certify connectivity without the connectedness premise. Cuts provide certificates of disconnection. In a simple nontrivial graph, vertex and edge connectivity cannot exceed minimum degree.

**Key relationship:** Σ degree(v) = 2|E|; edges in a forest = |V| − components

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. State directedness and simplicity.
2. Use paths or cuts as certificates.
3. Check edge-count extremes by constructing components.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Separate graph edges from traversal-forest edges. A forest on n vertices with c components has n−c edges, counting isolated vertices as components. For directed graphs distinguish reachability, weak connectivity and strong connectivity; replacing every directed edge by an undirected edge only tests weak connectivity.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
An undirected forest has 28 vertices and 19 edges. How many connected components does it have?

**Answer: 9.** Every tree component with vi vertices has vi−1 edges. Summing gives m=n−c, hence c=28−19=9. This formula applies because the graph is a forest; a graph with cycles can have additional edges without reducing its component count.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A bridge increases the number of components when removed. An articulation point is a vertex property; the two concepts are not interchangeable.

Exactly n − 1 edges does not imply a graph is a tree unless connectivity or acyclicity is also established.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

A connected simple undirected graph with n vertices and n−1 edges is:

- **A.** A tree
- **B.** A cycle
- **C.** Complete
- **D.** Always regular

**Answer: A.** A cycle edge could be removed without losing connectivity, contradicting the n−1 minimum. Thus it is a tree.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

For a tree on n≥2 vertices:

- **A.** There are n−1 edges
- **B.** Every edge is a bridge
- **C.** Every vertex is an articulation point
- **D.** Every pair has a unique simple path

**Answer: A, B, D.** A/B/D characterize trees. Leaves are not articulation points.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Maximum edges in a disconnected simple undirected graph on 6 vertices?



**Answer: 10.** A K₅ plus one isolated vertex maximizes edges: choose(5,2)=10. Splitting into more balanced components gives fewer.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2024 CS1 · Q60 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/graph-connectivity?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Graph connectivity. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Every connected component contributes a DFS tree. A tree with v vertices has v−1 edges.
2. Summing over c components and 100 vertices gives forest edges=100−c.
3. Since the forest has 40 edges, c=100−40=**60**, including any isolated-vertex components.
